{{Short description|Three-dimensional geometric shape}}
[[File:Kugelschale.svg|300px|thumb|spherical shell, right: two halves]]
In [[geometry]], a '''spherical shell''' (a '''[[Ball (mathematics)#Regions|ball shell]]''') is a generalization of an [[Annulus (mathematics)|annulus]] to three dimensions. It is the region of a [[ball (mathematics)|ball]] between two [[concentric]] [[sphere]]s of differing radii.<ref name="Wolfram"/>

==Volume==
The [[volume]] of a spherical shell is the difference between the enclosed volume of the outer sphere and the [[Sphere#Enclosed volume|enclosed volume of the inner sphere]]:
: <math>\begin{align}
V &= \tfrac43\pi R^3 - \tfrac43\pi r^3 \\[3mu]
  &= \tfrac43\pi \bigl(R^3 - r^3\bigr) \\[3mu]
  &= \tfrac43\pi (R-r)\bigl(R^2 + Rr + r^2\bigr)
\end{align}</math>
where {{mvar|r}} is the radius of the inner sphere and {{mvar|R}} is the radius of the outer sphere.

==Approximation==
An approximation for the volume of a thin spherical shell is the surface area of the inner sphere multiplied by the thickness {{mvar|t}} of the shell:<ref name="wonders"/>
: <math>V \approx 4 \pi r^2 t,</math>
when {{mvar|t}} is very small compared to {{mvar|r}} (<math>t \ll r</math>).         

The total surface area of the spherical shell is <math>4 \pi r^2</math>.
